validation.notes: Fixed two regressions in one pipeline. (1) packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts: migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot() had lost its destination guard and unconditionally renameSync()'d over an existing session file; restored `if (existsSync(newPath)) continue;` so existing destination bytes always win, the legacy source stays in place (both sides preserved) and the remaining legacy sessions in the same batch still migrate; re-running is idempotent. (2) packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts: loadEntriesFromFile() validated the header with `header.type !== "session" && typeof header.id !== "string"`, so a `type:"session"` header with a missing/numeric id passed and the reader then appended a newline to a file it had not accepted; changed the operator to `||`, matching parseSessionHeaderCandidate()/readSessionHeader() in the same module. The reader now rejects (returns []) without rewriting, while valid headers and valid unterminated final records are still loaded and terminated. Validation: .prale-eval/regression.mjs loads the real migrations.ts through its real fs boundary and the real session-manager.ts/ SessionManager (via the read-only subject.mjs link), creates fixtures under .prale-eval/tmp and removes them in a finally block. It asserts: colliding destination bytes unchanged, legacy source bytes preserved, non-colliding legacy file still migrated, migrated unterminated file loaded by the real reader and gain exactly one newline, numeric-id / missing-id / non-session unterminated files rejected as [] with byte-identical content, SessionManager.open throwing `not a valid ... session` without rewriting the file, and a valid unterminated session still loading 2 entries and gaining one newline while an already-terminated file is untouched. Mutation check (performed locally, then restored): restoring only migrations.ts to HEAD fails the destination-preservation assertion; restoring only session-manager.ts to HEAD fails the rejected-invalid-header assertion (2 vs 0 entries). Both are uncaught node:assert/strict failures, not crashes. Limitation: no node_modules in this workspace, so the repo's vitest suites (e.g. packages/coding-agent/test/session-manager/file-operations.test.ts) and tsc were not run; the regression script covers the affected reader/migration behavior directly against the real sources. No real time, randomness, network or credentials used.
